Kimberly / team,

I've done an initial pass on the redlines — attached is a short summary and suggested positions. High level thoughts:

MSA:
- Indemnity: Prospero expanded the third-party claim carveouts; propose we accept limited carveouts for open-source and pre-existing customer data but push back on broad platform-level carveouts.
- SLA & credits: We should not accept a 90-day remediation SLA as an availability SLA; recommend converting to a "security remediation reasonable effort and mitigation" clause with escalation & reporting cadence (30/60/90 checkpoints) and a defined maximum credit formula.

DPA:
- Telemetry/logs: ok to provide structured export via S3 (signed, auditable). Need to confirm retention windows and ability to purge on request — propose 45-day default retention for debug logs and 1 yr for aggregated metrics unless customer requests otherwise.
- Security obligations: counter to require evidence (attestation) rather than open audit access. We can offer SOC2 summaries and scoped audit support under NDA.

Procurement:
- Trial PO: we can accept a 60-day trial PO but recommend capping trial spend to $25k of committed usage or convert to trial credits; otherwise we risk open billing exposure.
- Payment terms: can move to net-45 for enterprise deals > $200k ARR; otherwise net-30 remains standard.

I've attached "Kimberly_Prospero_Redline_Summary.docx" (local). I'll sync with Legal on tracked-changes for the MSA/DPA.

Marissa
Director, Commercial Contracts

Thanks — quick commercial view:
- Prospero is strategic in Q3 pipeline (partner-led channel opportunity). We should be flexible on initial commercial asks to accelerate POC and marketplace listing. My recommendations: accept 60-day trial PO; agree to net-45 for the initial contract (with a clause to revert to net-30 on renewal). Also consider a one-time onboarding credit to offset any risk (e.g., $15k credit applied against first invoice).
- We should be firm on indemnity and data boundaries (Marissa's call).

If legal wants concessions on the SLA we should tie them to specific remediation workflows and a clear penalty structure limited to credits rather than unlimited liability.

I'll take point on the commercial offer once legal provides final text.

Subject: RE: Prospero - integration MSA/DPA redlines and procurement checklist — consolidated next steps

Thanks, Tina / Anna — consolidating our position and next steps below so everyone has a single action list. I'll attach the tracked-change package at the end of the day.

Summary of Redwood positions (proposed):
- Trial & billing: Agree to a 60-day trial PO for $20k to be applied to the first invoice. We will accept net-45 for this initial agreement. Onboarding credit: Redwood will provide a one-time $15k onboarding credit to be applied on first invoice.
- DPA / telemetry: We can deliver structured exports (CSV/Parquet) to a Prospero-owned S3 with signed transfer and retention controls. Standard retention: 12 months for raw logs, 18 months for aggregated metrics; we can shorten retention on request and will include purge procedures in the SOW.
- Security remediation SLA: Counterproposal — instead of a 90-day binding remediation SLA with credits, we propose a 30/60/90 remediation plan with status reporting and a defined credit cap tied to monthly recurring fees (not unlimited liability). We will offer SOC2 attestation and scoped audit support under NDA.
- Indemnity & liability: We will not accept broad platform carve-outs. Proposed language narrows indemnity for pre-existing customer data and open-source components.
- Procurement forms: We will provide vendor onboarding packet (W9, bank details) and standard vendor master documents. No additional Redwood-specific procurement forms required.

Action items / owners:
- Marissa: finalize MSA + DPA tracked changes and call out two points where legal must escalate (indemnity language + SLA credit cap). Due EOD 18-May.
- Monica: confirm technical export mechanism (S3 pattern, encryption at rest/in-transit) and provide SOW language for retention/purge. Due EOD 18-May.
- Jonas: prepare a commercial term sheet with trial PO details and onboarding credit. Due EOD 18-May.
- Kimberly: compile final packet, circulate to Prospero legal and procurement, and schedule a follow-up call (proposed 21-May).

Prospero questions that still need answers:
- Who signs invoices for net-45? (Jonas / Finance will confirm)
- Any additional compliance evidence required beyond SOC2? (Monica to confirm)

Thanks all — I’ll circulate the tracked-changes and a one-page mutual action plan after I receive the attachments from Marissa and Monica.

Best,
